findings.issue: No test script, no test runner, and no test files anywhere in app/ — the app relies entirely on the external acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest (or similar) with unit tests for src/lib/api.js's pure helpers and a few route-handler tests against fixture JSON, wired to a "test" script.

findings.issue: The alternate-form cutoff (id < 10000), Pokémon→species mapping, and dedup/sort in uniqueSpeciesFromPokemonReferences are the most reused and least guarded logic in the app.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with fixture URLs covering deoxys-normal (10001), duplicates, and out-of-order input; assert species mapping and dex ordering.

findings.issue: Pagination math (page clamp, slice bounds) and homeHref's rule of omitting default params are untested; 'Next page' links that drop active filters would slip through the acceptance fixtures.
findings.suggestion: Test the handler with parametrized query strings (out-of-range page, empty/unknown type, combined filters) and assert resulting props and hrefs.

findings.issue: Every error — including API 500s and network failures — is rendered as the 404 'Not found' page, masking real outages as missing data.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish ApiError.status === 404 from other failures (500 page or rethrow), and add tests asserting a 500 API response doesn't render 'Not found'.

findings.issue: The DOM sort comparator (missing-values-last in both directions, numeric vs text, aria-sort flip) is untested and easy to regress during a rewrite.
findings.suggestion: Extract compareRows/sorting into a testable module and unit-test missing values, numbers as strings, and direction toggling.

findings.issue: Method-table ordering (Level Up, Machine, Egg, Tutor, then others alphabetically) and the level-then-name default sort are untested; the acceptance suite only exercises Pikachu.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test orderedMethods construction and sortMoveRows with a synthetic method mix including an 'other' method.

findings.issue: The debounce/race guard (requestId) and DOM-swap refresh have no tests; dropping the stale-response guard produces flickering wrong results the acceptance suite may not reliably catch.
findings.suggestion: Add a small integration test (or extract the fetch-and-swap logic) covering rapid successive inputs and a slow second response arriving first.

findings.issue: Spec-critical formatting — whitespace collapse of flavor text (\n, \f), dex-number padding, em dash for nulls — is only pinned by the harness's specific fixtures.
findings.suggestion: Straightforward table-driven unit tests: humanize('mr-mime'), dexNumber(25), displayValue(null), flavor text with \f and trailing spaces.

findings.issue: The request cache's promise-based behavior (failed requests evicted so retries work, successes cached forever) is subtle and untested; a refactor to cache resolved values could break retry-after-failure.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with a stubbed fetch: failure then success returns data; success is not re-fetched.

findings.issue: Hidden-ability marking (is_hidden entries collected by id, then joined to species) has no test; a Pokémon with the ability both normally and hidden is an easy edge case to get wrong.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the mapping with a fixture where one Pokémon has the ability in both slots.

summary: The app ships zero tests of its own — no runner, no script, no test files — so all protection comes from the harness's acceptance suite, which the team won't control. This hurts more than usual because the code is cleanly modular: src/lib/api.js is a suite of pure functions that a day of unit tests would pin cheaply. Highest-value gaps are the alternate-form/species-mapping filters, home pagination and URL-param handling, the error paths that render every API failure as 'Not found', and the client-side table sorting.
